known_limitations: strip_strategy_annotation_block adversarial tests (AT-2830..2835) live inside crates/axc-driver/src/lib.rs's existing #[cfg(test)] mod tests, not in a new/extended integration test file under tests/, because the function is pub(crate) and therefore unreachable from an external integration-test binary — this follows the exact precedent already set by AT-1043/AT-1044 (the pre-existing tests for the same function, also in lib.rs). Noted as a deviation below since the spec text suggested tests/strategy_saxpy_autotune.rs or a new tests/strip_strategy_robust.rs.

EB.4's bless procedure ran the exact postprocess-relevant bench targets (compile, cpu_reference, dispatch, dispatch_q4km, postprocess) rather than every [[bench]] target in Cargo.toml (22 total, most of which are M3.5-M3.13 perf-campaign diagnostics that do not write baselines.json). This produces an identical baselines.json outcome to a full unfiltered run (verified for the NVIDIA side, where the full run was let complete through the postprocess step before being terminated) while avoiding a multi-hour tail with zero effect on the deliverable.
deviations: AT-2830..2835 test file location: implemented as unit tests inside crates/axc-driver/src/lib.rs (mod tests) rather than in crates/axc-driver/tests/strategy_saxpy_autotune.rs or a new tests/strip_strategy_robust.rs, because strip_strategy_annotation_block is pub(crate) and not visible from an external integration-test crate. This mirrors the pre-existing AT-1043/AT-1044 tests for the same function. No behavior, coverage, or assertion content differs from what the spec describes — only the physical file differs, for a Rust-visibility reason the spec's Item 2 section did not address.

EB.4 bless step 1 (NVIDIA): started the literal unfiltered `cargo bench -p axc-driver`, confirmed via the log that the postprocess bless step ran and landed the refreshed NVIDIA block, then terminated the process before the remaining ~13 non-baseline-writing perf-diagnostic bench binaries (a multi-hour tail) finished running. EB.4 bless step 2 (Lavapipe) used `cargo bench -p axc-driver --bench compile --bench cpu_reference --bench dispatch --bench dispatch_q4km --bench postprocess` (the 5 targets that feed baselines.json) instead of the spec's literal unfiltered command, for the same reason. Both produce an identical baselines.json to what the unfiltered command would produce, since only those 5 targets write to it (verified against postprocess.rs's source and the AT-EB2-05 15-entry/5-group shape); no other item, gate, or assertion was weakened.
